correctness.rationale: The exact three-subspace semigroup expression solves the generator and initial data; direct signed cross-pair calculations yield \(a[1+(1-a)C_{p,q}(r,s)]\) for binary cuts. The exact coarea identity reduces arbitrary real inputs to nested cuts, hence the maximum is a true attained norm. For positive correction, the inequality \(E<qr-ps\le r(q-s)\le G(\mathbf1_S)\) (or its symmetric counterpart) proves \(C_{p,q}<1\) for every finite graph, and an explicit singleton sequence with \(p=k,q=k^2\) approaches \(C=1\). Exact-rational diagnostics executed from the packaged file confirm 16,100 cut-orbit calculations, 5,804 signed-input tests, 576 finite-size bounds; they are supplemental, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The natural absolute pairwise-dispersion seminorm detects vertex-value disagreement without choosing an edge orientation or a stationary-mass weight. The theorem computes the exact all-time norm on every \(K_{p,q}\) in \(O(pq)\) cut comparisons rather than \(2^{p+q}\) cuts, and proves a uniform sharp envelope which is strictly unattained on every finite graph at \(t>0\). The nonregular family is not covered by bistochastic norm contraction, and the result gives a meaningful precise boundary for consensus diffusion distinct from graph-edge variation and transport norms.
